findings.judgment: The modern biography now gives1789, matching the initial first-party Deutsches Museum collection identity. The single block numeric replacement declares1787-to1789 with archival provenance and context-number. The original source, embedded source snapshot and faithful source_text are unchanged. No formula, mathematical erratum or unrelated numeral changed. This resolves both the factual error and the required explicit source/modern divergence.

The revised relation explicitly says proportionality can be approximate in an appropriate limited temperature range where sensitivity varies very little. It no longer asserts exact proportionality in Ohm's actually used range. This matches the initial independent reasoning: thermocouple emf integrates differential sensitivity, so approximately constant sensitivity permits a local approximate proportionality, whereas the reused NIST higher-order reference functions exclude a general exact finite-range claim. The temperature-difference control idea and dissimilar-metal source remain; no actual historical interval, tolerance, Type T/Type J apparatus assignment or particular metals are invented.

The corrected sentence specifies a low-resistance conductor directly joining the supply's two terminals and bypassing the original load. That topology distinguishes the hazardous bridge from a normal low-resistance lead in series with a lamp, resolving the initial counterexample. The thermal/chemical/magnetic effects still require their respective laws, and the unchanged next paragraph retains formula reference(9-3), possible large current and serious consequences. It does not claim every connecting wire is a short circuit or that current is infinite.
